definitions.explanation: The third day of any month.

examples.japanese: 1{月|がつ}{三日|みっか}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{三日|みっか}{後|ご}に{届|とど}きます。
examples.english: It will arrive in three days.

examples.japanese: {三日|みっか}は{忙|いそが}しいです。
{三日|みっか}も{雨|あめ}が{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: It rained for three days straight.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}{三日|みっか}に{予約|よやく}した。
examples.english: I made a reservation for the 3rd of next month.

examples.japanese: {三日|みっか}{間|かん}の{出張|しゅっちょう}です。
{三日|みっか}までに{返事|へんじ}します。
{三日|みっか}{坊主|ぼうず}で{終|お}わった。
examples.english: It ended after just three days (gave up quickly).

examples.japanese: {三日|みっか}は{空|あ}いていますか。

notes:
{三日|みっか} has two meanings: a duration of three days, and the 3rd day of the month. Context usually makes the meaning clear.

DAYS OF THE MONTH (1-10):
- {一日|ついたち}, {二日|ふつか}, {三日|みっか}, {四日|よっか}, {五日|いつか}
- {六日|むいか}, {七日|なのか}, {八日|ようか}, {九日|ここのか}, {十日|とおか}

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {三日|みっか}{間|かん}: three days (with counter)
- {三日|みっか}{後|ご}: three days later
- {三日|みっか}{前|まえ}: three days ago

IDIOM:
{三日|みっか}{坊主|ぼうず} literally "three-day monk" means someone who gives up easily or lacks perseverance. Used when someone starts something but quickly abandons it.
